newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle seen firm Thursday - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle seen firm Thursday - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Thursday were seen steady-firm in active trading following the New Year's holiday on Wednesday, according to feedlot sources.
There were light sales Tuesday at $67.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from last week's high, but the volume was too thin for an adequate market test, the sources said.

About 1,000 head of steers and heifers grading select and choice were sold in Kansas, according to USDA and private sources. There were no reported sales from Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots, they said.
The cattle sold in Kansas reportedly came from one feedlot and were being shipped to Nebraska, feedlot sources said.
Remaining feedlots reportedly did not see aggressive bids from packers at the $67.00 level but fully expect brisk trade at that level on Thursday, they said.
Fed cattle prices were expected to be underpinned by ideas that several packers were short on slaughter inventory.
Gains could be muted by sentiment that retailer buying was near complete for first-half January promotions.
Beef prices at midday closed down $0.82 to $0.85 for choice cuts and up $0.06 to $0.09 for selects on 180 fabricated loads.
